spine: Every week you water your fern.
You never see where the water goes.
Until the pot is cut in half.
Because of that, you see the top soil soak it up and the roots drink.
Because of that, you see the extra sink through the gravel and drain into the saucer.
Until finally you know why feed goes in the water, at the dose per litre.

scores.note: A plain question over a half-cut pot; the camera is moving from frame one.
Question, soil, roots, drainage, tag: a chain rather than a drama, as the format intends.
No character: the viewer is the character. An explainer trades this rule for curiosity.
The cutaway makes the per-litre dose make sense, but the product only appears on the end card.
Reveal and tag only, by design: an explainer that sells in the middle stops being trusted.
Plain horticulture, no promise about results; one label claim.

output.verdict: A clean explainer that does its job and sells softly; score it on watch time and saves rather than on the story-ad rules.
fixes: Lengthen to 45-75 s with three more stops (overwatering, a pot with no hole, the feed dose) to match the format's real length.
Put the bottle on the ledge from the first frame as a quiet plant.
Add one recurring small prop (a fallen leaf riding the water) for continuity.
output.reason: The story-ad rules undervalue an explainer by design (no character, a late product); as an explainer it reads clearly and honestly.
